@Misiu According to your log, it seems that you've set up a lot of ping binary sensors. Since the ping component uses `update` instead of the async version `async_update`, the updates cannot be running in parallel ([see here](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data#request-parallelism)). Therefore, all those binary sensors have to update one by one and they eventually go pass the 30 seconds interval. We'll need to refactor the integration into a async one to truly solve this problem. For now, you can try to increase the update interval and / or set the `count` option to a smaller number.

@Misiu Refactoring shouldn't be difficult since it is a relatively small integration. If you feel you wanna try, [this](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-subprocess.html) could be helpful, which is an async version of the `subprocess` module used in the integration.

I've also noticed his in logs:
```
2020-05-06 11:16:56 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.binary_sensor] Setup of binary_sensor platform ping is taking over 10 seconds.
```

@shenxn sadly ping has no tests so I can't test if my changes work correctly :/
Also, I'm not a Python expert.
This is my changed binary_sensor: https://github.com/Misiu/home-assistant/blob/async_ping/homeassistant/components/ping/binary_sensor.py
Could you take a look?
@Misiu You are on the right track. Only a few things need to be changed. Just create a pull request so I can make a review.
But, why is this suddenly requiring a rewrite after it worked fine for years?

@atpage The problem is there for a long time, but it only happens when you have many ping sensors and a pretty short scan interval. Also, there is only going to be a lot of warning messages and nothing actually break.

Hmm, so does this not have the same cause as issue [33281](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/33281)?  nmap_tracker has been throwing the same errors as the ping tracker, but it started suddenly in the last few months with no change to config.
@atpage They can have the same cause if there was something changed in how homeassistant handles integration polling. But I don't know much about that so I'm not pretty sure.

review_comments:
Spawning a subprocess with inactive current child watcher raises `RuntimeError`.

We always have a child watcher so that shouldn't ever been an issue.
